title: state-machine
description: The life cycle of one entity as states and transitions, laid out as a diagram. States with no way in from an initial state are flagged “unreachable”, non-final states with no way out “dead end”. Each transition with an anchor is content-checked: the anchored line must contain the name of the target state (`to`), otherwise the transition is shown as inferred. On explain-pr pages mark parts with `change` (and `before` on changed transitions) to get Before / After / Diff. Not rendered when `states` is empty.

id.description: The state as the code names it (`paid`); transitions refer to it, the content check looks for it. Part id.

label.description: Human name of the state; defaults to the id.

initial.description: The entity starts here. Mark at least one state initial, or reachability is not checked.

final.description: The life cycle may end here; a final state is never a dead end.

text.description: One line about the state, shown on hover.

id.description: Part id, unique in the block; a route step can focus it.

to.description: The `id` of the target state; the anchored line must contain it.

trigger.description: The event or call that fires the transition (`refund`).

condition.description: The guard that must hold, in a few words (`within 14 days of delivery`).

anchor.description: The line that performs the transition and names the target state. A line without the target state demotes the transition to inferred.

trigger.description: Old trigger; "" when the transition had none.

condition.description: Old guard; "" when the transition had none (the PR added it).

anchor.description: Into the base repo (`<repo>@base`). Its line must contain `before.to`, so give `before.to` (even when unchanged) whenever you give `before.anchor`; otherwise the old transition is shown as inferred in Before. A changed `before.to` without `before.anchor` is shown as inferred, with no code chip.
